ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the square metal coil abcd is laid flat on a rough horizontal conveyor belt, driven by an electric motor to move together at a uniform speed v. The side length of the coil is L, its resistance is R, and its mass is m. There is a square magnetic field with boundary length 2L perpendicular to the conveyor belt, and the magnetic induction intensity is B. During the process in which the coil passes through the magnetic field region, its speed remains unchanged. Which of the following statements is correct? (　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, the square metal coil abcd is laid flat on a rough horizontal conveyor belt, driven by an electric motor to move together at a uniform speed v. The side length of the coil is L, its resistance is R, and its mass is m. There is a square magnetic field with boundary length 2L perpendicular to the conveyor belt, and the magnetic induction intensity is B. When the coil comes out of the magnetic field, in what direction does the induced current flow?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a square metal coil on the conveyor belt, with vertices labeled in sequence as lower-left a, lower-right b, upper-right c, and upper-left d; the conveyor belt velocity v points to the right. The dashed box on the right represents the square magnetic field region. In the figure, the magnetic induction intensity B is represented by upward arrows, that is, upward perpendicular to the conveyor belt. Reasoning: The coil moves to the right with the conveyor belt. When the coil comes out of the magnetic field, the original magnetic flux through the coil is decreasing. According to Lenz's law, the magnetic field produced by the induced current should hinder this decrease, so the direction of the induced magnetic field should be the same as the direction of the original magnetic field B in the figure, still upward perpendicular to the conveyor belt. Then, by the right-hand screw rule, when the thumb points in the direction of B in the figure, the direction in which the four fingers curl corresponds to the current direction in the coil as a→b→c→d→a. Therefore, the induced current flows along the abcda direction.
